spacr.architecture_training:
Train the spaCR channel-adaptive architectures from settings: well sets, cells, pre-training, missing stains.

One settings file runs one of two levels (``train_level``):

* ``'well_set'``: the :class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer`
  on per-cell embeddings, scored by mechanism of action with its ablations
  and controls (:func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`).
* ``'cell'``: the channel-adaptive CNN or ViT (``train_arch``) on single-cell
  crops (:func:`run_cell_architecture`). Optionally the ViT is first
  pre-trained without labels (``pretrain_method``: ``'mae'``, He et al.
  2022, or ``'dino'``, Caron et al. 2021) for ``pretrain_epochs`` epochs;
  ``train_labels_per_class`` then keeps only that many labelled cells per
  class (few-shot). Every model is scored on the full stain panel and on
  each subset of ``eval_channel_subsets`` (the missing-stain evaluation),
  beside a majority-class control and, with ``train_set_shuffle_control``, a
  model trained on shuffled labels.

Cell crops come as one ``(cells, channels, height, width)`` array
(``train_cell_crops``, ``.npy``) with a row-aligned table
(``train_cell_table``) holding the label and the group (well) column; cells
are split by group, so no well is in both training and test. The crops are
raw: each channel is divided by the 99th percentile of up to 2,048 training
crops, clipped at 1.5 and mapped by ``(x - 0.5) / 0.25``, the transform of
the gene-class benchmark. Training augments by flips, 90-degree rotations and
a per-channel gain within 10%.

``spacr-run spacr_architectures`` and ``python -m
spacr.architecture_training --settings file.csv`` run it headless.

The settings of :func:`run_spacr_architectures`, filled in with their defaults.

:param settings: settings given so far; a key already present is kept.

:param value: the setting, or a list of lists.

Keep at most ``per_class`` training cells of each class.

:param rows: the training rows.
:param labels: the class index of every cell.
:param per_class: cells kept per class; 0 or less keeps all.
:param seed: seed of the draw.
:returns: the kept rows, sorted.

Per-channel scale: the 99th percentile of up to ``sample`` crops of ``rows``.

:param crops: crops shaped ``(cells, channels, height, width)``.
:param rows: the crops the scale may look at (the training cells).
:param sample: most crops read.
:param seed: seed of the draw.

Run :func:`run_spacr_architectures` from a settings file.

``python -m spacr.architecture_training --settings file.csv`` reads the
settings file with :func:`spacr.cli.load_settings_file`.

:param argv: the arguments; None reads :data:`sys.argv`.

spacr.architecture_training.predict_cell:
Predicted class of each cell, optionally with only a subset of the stains.

:param model: the trained classifier.
:param crops: raw crops.
:param rows: the cells to predict.
:param scale: the per-channel scale.
:param size: input size.
:param subset: stains kept (the others treated as missing); None keeps the training panel.
:param batch: cells per forward pass.
:returns: the class index of each cell.
spacr.architecture_training.prepare_batc:
Turn raw crops into model input, with augmentation when a generator is given.

``((x / scale).clip(0, 1.5) - 0.5) / 0.25``, bilinear resize to ``size``;
with ``generator``, a random flip, a random 90-degree rotation (one per
batch) and a per-channel gain within 10% (per crop).

:param crops: crops shaped ``(cells, channels, height, width)``.
:param rows: the crops of the batch.
:param scale: the per-channel scale (:func:`fixed_channel_scale`).
:param size: output size.
:param generator: torch generator of the augmentation; None for none.
:returns: the ``(len(rows), channels, size, size)`` float tensor.
spacr.architecture_training.pretrain_enc:
Pre-train a channel ViT without labels, in place.

MAE: the encoder's own channel dropout is off (the MAE masks whole
stains itself). DINO: an EMA teacher (momentum 0.996 rising to 1 on a
cosine) sees two random resized views; the student also drops stains.
AdamW with the reference learning rate scaled by ``batch / 256`` and
gradient clipping at 3.

:param enc: the encoder; its weights are updated (DINO keeps the student's).
:param crops: raw crops shaped ``(cells, channels, height, width)``.
:param rows: the cells used (labels are never read).
:param scale: the per-channel scale.
:param method: ``'mae'`` or ``'dino'``.
:param epochs: passes over ``rows``.
:param batch: cells per step.
:param mask_ratio: MAE masking ratio.
:param lr: base learning rate for a batch of 256.
:param seed: seed of the batches and the augmentation.
:param size: input size; None uses the encoder's.
:returns: the loss of every step.
:raises ValueError: an unknown method.
spacr.architecture_training.run_cell_arc:
Train and score a channel-adaptive CNN or ViT on cell crops from settings.

Writes ``<dst>/summary.csv`` (one row per model and stain subset, the
shuffled-label control when asked, and the majority-class control),
``glossary.json``, ``config.json``, ``losses.json`` and ``model.pt`` (the
trained classifier's state dict).

:param settings: the keys of :func:`architecture_defaults`.
:returns: dict with ``summary`` (the frame) and ``paths``.
:raises ValueError: a blank input, an architecture that is not an image
    model, pre-training on the CNN, or a crops/table length mismatch.
spacr.architecture_training.run_spacr_ar:
Run the level ``train_level`` names from settings.

:param settings: the keys of :func:`architecture_defaults`.
:returns: the result of :func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`
    (``'well_set'``) or of :func:`run_cell_architecture` (``'cell'``).
:raises ValueError: an unknown level or architecture.
spacr.architecture_training.split_by_gro:
Split cells into training and test rows so that no group is in both.

:param groups: the group of each cell (such as its well).
:param test_fraction: share of the groups held out, at least one.
:param seed: seed of the permutation of the sorted groups.
:returns: the training rows and the test rows.
:raises ValueError: fewer than two groups.
spacr.architecture_training.train_cell_c:
Train a :class:`spacr.channel_models.ChannelClassifier` on labelled cells, in place.

Batches are drawn with replacement, class-balanced; cross-entropy with
label smoothing 0.1, AdamW (weight decay 0.05), :func:`spacr.well_set_training.cosine_schedule`
and gradient clipping at 1.

:param model: the classifier.
:param crops: raw crops.
:param rows: the labelled training cells.
:param labels: the class index of every cell.
:param scale: the per-channel scale.
:param size: input size.
:param epochs: passes over ``rows``.
:param batch: cells per step.
:param lr: learning rate.
:param seed: seed of the batches and the augmentation.
:returns: the loss of every step.
spacr.channel_models:
Channel-adaptive models for any stain panel: a CNN, a ViT and a well set transformer.

All three models take any number of channels (1 to more than 10) with the
same weights. Every channel is processed on its own and tagged with a learned
stain embedding, looked up by stain name rather than by slot index, so
BBBC021 "DNA" and an OPS "DAPI" share one vector and an unseen panel still
runs.

* :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` is a channel-adaptive ConvNeXt-style CNN: a
  HyperNet stem per channel, ConvNeXt blocks shared across channels and
  FiLM-conditioned on the stain, cross-channel attention at every spatial
  location (one feature map per channel is kept) and channel attention
  pooling at the end, which records the stain that drove the call.
* :class:`SpacrChannelViT` is a channel-aware ViT: per-channel patch tokens
  plus a stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position, an optional per-sample
  channel-availability mask for missing stains, and Hierarchical Channel
  Sampling (channel dropout, Bao et al. 2024) in training. It is pre-trained
  with :class:`ChannelMAE` (He et al. 2022) or :class:`ChannelDINO` (Caron et
  al. 2021).
* :class:`SpacrWellTransformer` is a set model over the single-cell
  embeddings of a well. Mode ``'arrayed'``: an ISAB set encoder (Lee et al.
  2019) and gated multi-head attention-MIL pooling (Ilse et al. 2018) give
  the well logits, the attention weights and per-cell instance logits (the
  penetrant fraction, :func:`penetrant_fraction`). Mode ``'pooled'``: per-cell
  logits conditioned on a context set of other cells of the same well; an
  empty context is a learned null token, so the no-context ablation is the
  same model with set size 0.

:func:`build_channel_model` is the registry: it builds any of the three by
the name in :data:`CHANNEL_ARCHITECTURES`, which is also what the train
setting ``train_arch`` and :func:`spacr.utils.choose_model` accept.
:class:`ChannelClassifier` gives the two image models the ``model(x) ->
logits`` interface of the rest of spaCR's train path.

Inputs are expected already normalised by the benchmark transform,
``((x / scale).clip(0, 1.5) - 0.5) / 0.25``. The models use plain torch
modules and no BatchNorm, so a step with a zero learning rate leaves every
weight unchanged.
spacr.channel_models.Block:
Pre-norm transformer block with a key-padding mask and layer scale.

With ``kv`` given it is a cross-attention block (queries ``x``, keys and
values ``kv``).

:param dim: token dimension.
:param heads: attention heads.
:param mlp: MLP expansion ratio.
:param drop_path: stochastic depth rate.
:param ls_init: initial layer scale.
:param dropout: attention and MLP dropout.
:param cross: add a LayerNorm on the keys and values.
Build the norms, the projections and the MLP.
spacr.channel_models.Block.attn:
Multi-head attention of ``x`` over ``kv``.

:param x: queries shaped ``(B, N, D)``.
:param kv: keys and values shaped ``(B, M, D)``.
:param mask: ``(B, M)`` booleans, True to attend; a row with nothing
    to attend to gives a zero output instead of NaN.
:param need_weights: also return the attention weights.
:returns: the projected output and the ``(B, heads, N, M)`` weights, or None.
spacr.channel_models.Block.forward:
Apply the block.

:param x: tokens shaped ``(B, N, D)``.
:param kv: keys and values for cross-attention; None attends to ``x``.
:param mask: key-padding mask, True to attend.
:param need_weights: also return the attention weights.
:returns: the updated tokens, or the tokens and weights with ``need_weights``.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelClassifier:
An image model of this module with a linear head: ``model(x) -> logits``.

This is the interface the rest of spaCR's train path expects. The channel
subsets of the missing-stain evaluation are applied here too:
``train_subset`` in training, ``eval_subset`` at test time (falling back
to ``train_subset``).

:param enc: a :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` or :class:`SpacrChannelViT`.
:param num_classes: classes of the head.
:param stains: stain names of the input channels; None uses the encoder's.
:param train_subset: stains kept in training; None keeps all.
:param eval_subset: stains kept at test time; None keeps ``train_subset``.
:param head_dropout: dropout before the head.
Build the head and resolve the channel subsets to slot indices.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelClassifier.e:
The encoder embedding of a batch, after the channel subset.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:returns: the ``(B, num_features)`` embedding.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelClassifier.f:
Class logits of a batch.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:returns: ``(B, num_classes)`` logits.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelClassifier.s:
Set the stains kept in training and at test time.

:param train_subset: stain names kept in training; None keeps all.
:param eval_subset: stain names kept at test time; None keeps ``train_subset``.
:raises ValueError: a subset names a stain the model's channels do not have.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelDINO:
DINO self-distillation (Caron et al. 2021) for the channel ViT.

Student and EMA teacher see two augmented views of the same cell; the
student, in training mode, also sees a random channel subset of its view,
so the embedding learns to stay the same when stains are missing. The
loss is the cross-entropy between the sharpened, centred teacher and the
student prototype distributions.

:param enc_student: the encoder trained.
:param enc_teacher: an encoder of the same shape; it starts as a copy.
:param out: prototypes.
:param t_student: student temperature.
:param t_teacher: teacher temperature.
:param center_m: momentum of the teacher centre.
Build the heads and copy the student into the frozen teacher.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelDINO.ema:
Move the teacher towards the student.

:param m: momentum; the teacher keeps ``m`` of itself.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelDINO.forward:
The self-distillation loss of two views.

:param v1: the first view, images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:param v2: the second view, same shape.
:param stains: stain names of the channels; None uses the student's.
:returns: the scalar loss.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelMAE:
Masked autoencoder (He et al. 2022) on channel-patch tokens.

``mask_ratio`` of all ``C * N`` tokens is masked at random, and with
probability ``p_whole_channel`` per sample one whole channel is masked in
addition, so the model learns to predict one stain from the others. One
decoder is shared by all channels; the stain embedding tells it which to
paint. The loss is the mean squared error on the masked patches, each
patch normalised to zero mean and unit variance.

:param enc: the encoder to pre-train.
:param dec_dim: decoder dimension.
:param dec_depth: decoder blocks.
:param dec_heads: decoder heads.
:param mask_ratio: share of tokens masked.
:param p_whole_channel: probability of masking one whole channel too.
Build the decoder around ``enc``.
spacr.channel_models.ChannelMAE.forward:
The reconstruction loss of one batch.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:param stains: stain names of the channels; None uses the encoder's.
:returns: the scalar loss.
spacr.channel_models.ConvNeXtBlock:
ConvNeXt block (Liu et al. 2022) with FiLM from the stain embedding.

Depth-wise 7x7 convolution, LayerNorm, FiLM, a 4x MLP with GELU and a
layer scale, with a residual connection. The FiLM lets the channel-shared
weights specialise per stain; it starts at zero, so a new block is a
plain ConvNeXt block.

:param dim: feature dimension.
:param stain_dim: stain embedding dimension.
:param drop_path: stochastic depth rate.
:param ls_init: initial layer scale.
Build the convolution, the FiLM projection and the MLP.
spacr.channel_models.ConvNeXtBlock.forwa:
Apply the block.

:param x: per-channel feature maps shaped ``(B * C, D, h, w)``.
:param s: the stain embedding of each map, shaped ``(B * C, stain_dim)``.
:returns: the updated maps, same shape as ``x``.
spacr.channel_models.CrossChannelMix:
Self-attention across the channel tokens at every spatial location.

The feature maps stay per channel, so channel identity is kept. The cost
is linear in pixels and quadratic only in the channel count.

:param dim: feature dimension.
:param stain_dim: stain embedding dimension.
:param heads: attention heads.
:param ls_init: initial layer scale.
Build the projections.
spacr.channel_models.CrossChannelMix.for:
Mix the channels.

:param x: per-channel feature maps shaped ``(B * C, D, h, w)``.
:param s: the stain embeddings, shaped ``(C, stain_dim)``.
:param B: batch size.
:param C: channel count.
:param avail: ``(B, C)`` booleans, True for a present channel; None treats all as present.
:returns: the mixed maps, same shape as ``x``.
spacr.channel_models.DINOHead:
DINO projection head: a 3-layer MLP, L2 normalisation and a weight-normalised prototype layer.

:param dim: input dimension.
:param out: prototypes.
:param hidden: MLP hidden size.
:param bottleneck: MLP output size.
Build the MLP and the prototype layer.
spacr.channel_models.DINOHead.forward:
Prototype scores of a batch of embeddings.

:param x: embeddings shaped ``(B, dim)``.
:returns: ``(B, out)`` scores.
spacr.channel_models.DropPath:
Stochastic depth: drop a whole residual branch per sample in training.

:param p: drop probability.
Store the drop probability.
spacr.channel_models.DropPath.forward:
Return ``x`` with whole samples zeroed at rate ``p`` and the rest rescaled.

:param x: the branch output; the first axis is the sample axis.
:returns: a tensor shaped like ``x``.
spacr.channel_models.GatedAttentionPool:
Gated multi-head attention pooling (Ilse et al. 2018).

:param dim: token dimension.
:param hidden: hidden size of the gate.
:param heads: pooling heads.
:param dropout: dropout on the gate.
Build the two gate projections and the head projection.
Pool a set of tokens.

:param x: tokens shaped ``(B, N, D)``.
:param mask: ``(B, N)`` booleans, True for a valid token; None keeps all.
:returns: the pooled ``(B, heads * D)`` tensor and the ``(B, heads, N)`` weights;
    a row with no valid token gets zero weights.
spacr.channel_models.HyperStem:
Per-channel patchify stem whose one-channel kernel is generated from the stain.

``W_c = W_0 + MLP(e_c)`` (HyperNet, the best from-scratch adaptive CNN on
CHAMMI, Chen et al. 2023). The MLP starts at zero, so every stain starts
with the shared kernel.

:param dim: output feature dimension.
:param stain_dim: stain embedding dimension.
:param k: kernel size and stride.
Build the shared kernel, its bias and the HyperNet.
spacr.channel_models.HyperStem.forward:
Patchify every channel with its own kernel.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:param s: the stain embeddings, shaped ``(C, stain_dim)``.
:returns: feature maps shaped ``(B * C, dim, H / k, W / k)``.
spacr.channel_models.ISAB:
Induced set attention block (Lee et al. 2019, Set Transformer).

``m`` inducing points attend to the set and the set attends back, so the
cost is ``O(N m)`` instead of ``O(N ** 2)`` and a well of 1,000 cells is cheap.

:param dim: token dimension.
:param heads: attention heads.
:param m: inducing points.
:param dropout: attention and MLP dropout.
:param drop_path: stochastic depth rate.
Build the inducing points and the two cross-attention blocks.
spacr.channel_models.ISAB.forward:
Encode a set.

:param x: tokens shaped ``(B, N, D)``.
:param mask: ``(B, N)`` booleans, True for a valid token.
:returns: the encoded set, same shape as ``x``.
spacr.channel_models.LayerNorm2d: LayerNorm over the channel axis of a ``(B, D, H, W)`` feature map.
spacr.channel_models.LayerNorm2d.forward:
Normalise every pixel's feature vector.

:param x: feature map shaped ``(B, D, H, W)``.
:returns: the normalised map, same shape.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelCNN:
spaCR channel-adaptive CNN.

Default size: dims (32, 64, 128, 256), depths (2, 2, 4, 2), about 2.4 M
parameters. Height and width must be divisible by 32 (96, 128 and 224 all
work). In training, with ``channel_dropout``, a random channel subset is
kept per batch (the ``always_keep`` stains are never dropped). At test
time ``eval_channel_subset`` keeps only the named stains, the
missing-stain evaluation.

:param stains: stain names of the input channels in order.
:param dims: feature dimension per stage.
:param depths: blocks per stage.
:param stain_dim: stain embedding dimension.
:param drop_path: largest stochastic depth rate.
:param mix_heads: heads of the cross-channel mixing.
:param channel_dropout: Hierarchical Channel Sampling in training.
:param always_keep: stains never dropped.
:param num_classes: classes of the attached head; 0 attaches none.
:param head_dropout: dropout before the head.
Build the stem, the stages, the mixing layers and the channel pooling.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelCNN.cla:
Class logits from the attached head.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:param stains: stain names of the channels; None uses the model's.
:param avail: optional ``(B, C)`` channel-availability mask.
:returns: ``(B, num_classes)`` logits.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelCNN.for:
Embed a batch of images.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:param stains: stain names of the channels; None uses the model's.
:param avail: ``(B, C)`` booleans, True for a present channel. With a
    mask, no channel is dropped or selected, and the absent ones are zeroed.
:returns: the ``(B, dims[-1])`` embedding. ``last_channel_weights``
    holds the channel attention, which stain drove the embedding.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelViT:
spaCR channel-aware ViT.

Tokens: one shared one-channel patch embedding per channel, plus the
stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position shared over channels, so
``C * (img / patch) ** 2`` tokens and a CLS token. Default img 224 and
patch 32 (49 tokens per channel). The native-resolution arm is img 96 /
patch 12 (OPS) or img 128 / patch 16 (BBBC021). With
``bag_of_channels`` every channel is a separate sequence and the
per-channel CLS vectors are fused late, which is cheaper and the better
self-supervised setting on CHAMMI-75.

:param stains: stain names of the input channels in order.
:param img: input size; other sizes are resized to it.
:param patch: patch size; ``img`` must be divisible by it.
:param size: ``'tiny'``, ``'small'`` or ``'mini'`` (:data:`VIT_SIZES`).
:param dim: embedding dimension; None takes the size's.
:param depth: blocks; None takes the size's.
:param heads: heads; None takes the size's.
:param drop_path: largest stochastic depth rate.
:param channel_dropout: Hierarchical Channel Sampling in training.
:param always_keep: stains never dropped.
:param num_classes: classes of the attached head; 0 attaches none.
:param head_dropout: dropout before the head.
:param bag_of_channels: encode every channel on its own.
Build the patch and stain embeddings, the blocks and the channel pooling.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelViT.cla:
Class logits from the attached head.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:param stains: stain names of the channels; None uses the model's.
:param avail: optional ``(B, C)`` channel-availability mask.
:returns: ``(B, num_classes)`` logits.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelViT.enc:
Run the blocks over a token sequence with a CLS token in front.

:param t: tokens shaped ``(B, L, D)``.
:param mask: ``(B, L)`` booleans, True for a valid token.
:returns: the normalised ``(B, L + 1, D)`` sequence, CLS first.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelViT.for:
Embed a batch of images.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``.
:param stains: stain names of the channels; None uses the model's.
:param avail: ``(B, C)`` booleans, True for a present channel; the
    tokens of absent channels are masked out.
:returns: the ``(B, 2 * dim)`` embedding: CLS (or the channel mean
    with ``bag_of_channels``) and the channel attention pool.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelViT.tok:
Per-channel patch tokens with position and stain embeddings.

:param x: images shaped ``(B, C, H, W)``; resized to ``img`` when needed.
:param stains: stain names of the channels.
:returns: tokens shaped ``(B, C, N, D)``.
spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransforme:
spaCR well transformer over single-cell embeddings.

* ``'arrayed'``: ``forward(cells, mask)`` returns a dict with ``logits``
  ``(B, K)``, ``attn`` ``(B, pool_heads, N)``, ``cell_logits`` ``(B, N, K)``
  and ``well_emb``. A set size of 1 is the no-context ablation (a
  single-cell model); ``depth=0`` is plain attention-MIL.
* ``'pooled'``: ``forward(targets, context, ctx_mask)`` returns ``logits``
  ``(B, T, K)``, ``ctx_attn`` and ``cell_emb``. Targets attend only to the
  context, never to each other or to themselves; the context must come
  from other cells of the same well. An empty context is the no-context
  ablation (a learned null token).

:param in_dim: dimension of the cell embeddings.
:param num_classes: classes.
:param mode: ``'arrayed'`` or ``'pooled'``.
:param dim: model dimension.
:param depth: ISAB blocks (and, pooled, decoder blocks).
:param heads: attention heads.
:param inducing: ISAB inducing points.
:param pool_heads: attention-MIL heads (arrayed).
:param dropout: attention and head dropout.
:param feat_dropout: dropout on the input embeddings.
:param drop_path: stochastic depth rate.
Build the input projection, the set encoder and the mode's head.

:param cells: cell embeddings shaped ``(B, N, in_dim)``.

:returns: dict with ``logits``, ``attn``, ``cell_logits`` and ``well_emb``.

Per-cell logits of target cells, conditioned on a context set.

:param targets: target cell embeddings shaped ``(B, T, in_dim)``.
:param context: context cell embeddings shaped ``(B, M, in_dim)``; None or ``M == 0`` is no context.
:param ctx_mask: ``(B, M)`` booleans, True for a real context cell.

spacr.channel_models.build_channel_model:

The nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 classifiers, built as CellProfiler Analyst builds them.

classifiers in its Classifier window. Eight are scikit-learn estimators that

:class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` fitted on the training data;

spacr.embedding_profiles:
Raw crop shards, pretrained-backbone embeddings, well embedding profiles and a well UMAP.

The computer-vision arm of the BBBC021 benchmark, from settings, in four
steps that :func:`run_embedding_profiles` runs in order:

1. :func:`write_crop_shard` cuts a fixed-size window around each chosen
   cell of a plate from its merged fields (:func:`spacr.crops.open_merged_field`),
   raw: never stretched per crop (item 772), optionally divided by the
   plate's saved flat field (``crop_illumination='gain_offset'``), with a
   bit-flag mask (1 this cell, 2 any nucleus, 4 another cell, 8 outside
   the field). At most ``crop_cap_per_well`` cells per well are drawn by
   ``numpy.random.default_rng(crop_seed)``, well by well in sorted order.
   One HDF5 shard per plate holds ``images`` and ``masks``, beside a
   ``.cells.parquet`` with one row per crop;
2. :func:`embed_crop_shard` encodes the masked crops with a pretrained
   backbone (:mod:`spacr.embeddings`), each channel alone, under one fixed
   scale per plate and channel (the 99th percentile of a 2,048-crop
   sample, item 410);
3. :func:`aggregate_embedding_wells` writes ``wells_median.parquet``,
   ``wells_mean.parquet`` and the control cells' percentiles in the layout
   of the feature aggregate (:func:`spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells`),
   so :func:`spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation` scores them unchanged;
4. :func:`well_umap` writes a UMAP (McInnes et al. 2018) of the wells.

spacr.gene_class_images:
Image-model arms of the gene-class and MoA benchmark: crops, samplers, the saved transform and the train loop.

This is the image half of item 889, ported from the BMC reanalysis
``gc_train.py`` so that a benchmark or pilot fold is a spaCR run. One fold:

1. the crops: :class:`MemmapCrops` (BBBC021, a ``(cells, H, W, C)`` uint16
   ``.npy`` with an index table holding ``scale0..`` per cell) or
   :class:`OpsCrops` (OPS, cell-masked TIFF crops in tar shards with
   ``.index.csv`` byte offsets and a per-plate scale file). Both divide by a
   fixed per-plate, per-channel scale and clip, so crops stay raw on disk;
2. the labels and folds: :func:`bbbc_fold_setup` (MoA classes and the
   NSCB / NSC folds of :func:`spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds`) or
   :func:`ops_fold_setup` (multi-label gene classes from the
   :mod:`spacr.gene_classes` tables, gene folds, decoy heads, the shuffled
   control and the per-gene loss weight);
3. the sampler (``train_balanced_sampling``): :class:`BalancedSampler`,
   class-uniform for BBBC021 and, for OPS, :func:`class_gene_sampler` (half
   the batch from positive genes, class then gene then cell; half from
   negative genes);
4. the model (``train_arch``, :data:`IMAGE_ARCHITECTURES`):
   :func:`build_image_model` with the first convolution adapted to the
   channel count (:func:`adapt_first_conv`);
5. the transform: :func:`transform_spec` records the whole preprocessing,
   which is saved with the fold and checked again before scoring
   (:func:`check_transform`, item 772). :class:`DevicePrep` applies it on the
   device, with the train-time augmentation (dihedral, shift of up to 4 px,
   per-channel gain 0.9 to 1.1);
6. :func:`train_image_fold` trains with AdamW and a cosine schedule (AMP on a
   GPU, micro-batch halving on out-of-memory) and scores the held-out cells;
   :func:`score_bbbc_run` scores a BBBC021 run per well and per treatment.

The config keys and seeds are the reference's (``seed + fold`` for torch,
the sampler and the augmentation), so a CPU fold with the same config draws
the same batches. :func:`run_gene_class_images` runs every fold from the
settings of :mod:`spacr.gene_classes` (``ml_model='image'``).

spacr.gene_classes:
Gene classes of a pooled screen, gene-grouped folds and the class-prediction benchmark.

A gene class is a set of screened genes that share an annotation: a kinase
group, family or subfamily (KinHub, Manning et al. 2002), a CORUM complex, a
KEGG pathway, a GO-slim biological process, or a direction of one of Funk et
al. 2022's per-gene feature scores. :func:`build_gene_classes` builds the
class table from versioned source files (md5 recorded), merges or drops
near-duplicate classes, and splits the genes into folds with multi-label
iterative stratification (Sechidis et al. 2011, :func:`grouped_multilabel_folds`),
so every class has members in every fold and no gene is in two folds.

:func:`train_gene_class_baseline` fits one logistic regression per class on a
gene-level feature table, fold by fold, with optional decoy heads (random
gene sets of the classes' sizes, the null of the discovery calls) and a
shuffled-class control. :func:`evaluate_gene_class_run` scores the
out-of-fold predictions: per-class AUROC and average precision with
bootstrap intervals, specificity against phenotype-positive and
overlapping-class non-members, and the two discovery lists (known members
with a new image phenotype; predicted new functions) at BH q < 0.05 against
the decoy heads.

With ``ml_model='image'`` the classes are learned from single-cell crops
instead, by an image model (``train_arch``) trained fold by fold with
:mod:`spacr.gene_class_images`, and scored by the same evaluation.

:func:`run_gene_classes` runs the whole chain from a settings file. Every
seed is the reference's: folds 0, control pseudo-genes 0, decoys 99, label
shuffle 1, bootstrap 0, each offset by ``train_seed``.

fusing screen-based and knowledge-based predictions and comparing them under
controls, on the gene graph's held-out-gene protocol (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`)
with the knowledge blocks of :mod:`spacr.gene_knowledge`:

* :func:`run_knn_stack`: per-block cosine averaged over the blocks both genes
  have, and a 25-nearest-neighbour similarity-weighted category vote, over
  arms of blocks (``k_*``) with their no-screen arms and their
  screen-shuffled controls (``shufOPS``: the ``ops`` rows permuted among
  library genes; ``shufScreen``: ``ops`` and the image blocks permuted with
  one permutation);
* :func:`train_gene_function`: the gene graph's GPS / LR trainer on the
  knowledge arms, with task-specific blocks (``_f<k>``, ``_time``) and the
  Foldseek edges as an extra message-passing edge type (``struct``);
* :func:`run_late_fusion`: the mean of z-scored score matrices of two runs,
  and the same with the screen model replaced by its shuffled run;
* :func:`evaluate_gene_function`: the gene graph metrics plus paralog-excluded
  link and category AUPRC, the results table, the paired fold deltas and the
  winner rule, fixed before the runs: an arm qualifies when it beats the
  screen-only reference and the knowledge-only model in at least 4 of 5
  folds and its screen-shuffled control loses in at least 4 of 5; a simpler
  qualifying arm within 0.005 of the best wins when it is not worse in at
  least 3 of 5 folds;
* :func:`explain_gene_function`: cross-fitted calibration, the decoy FDR and
  the hypothesis table for poorly characterised genes, each call explained
  from the inputs only (screen similarity to the class's training members,
  nearest member by sequence embedding, shared domains, structural hits);
* :func:`run_gene_function` runs them in order.

spacr.gene_graph:
Learn gene-gene links and gene-to-category membership from screen gene profiles.

An optical pooled screen gives one profile per gene. Whether those profiles
say something about gene function that the published interaction maps did
not already know is judged here by two protocols, each with its controls:

* the **time split**: the model is trained on the gene-gene edges known in
  2022 (STRING v11.5, BioGRID 4.4.214, CORUM 3.0) and scored on the edges
  added since (``gene_graph_new_edges``), among every gene pair that was not
  a 2022 edge;
* **held-out genes**: for fold ``k`` every edge and every category membership
  of the fold's genes is hidden; the model scores those genes against every
  gene and every category.

The steps, each callable on its own and all four in order by
:func:`run_gene_graph` (what ``spacr-run gene_graph`` calls):

* :func:`build_gene_graph` assembles the nodes (screen genes and
  non-targeting pseudo-genes), the feature blocks with their missing
  indicators, the typed edges, the categories and the folds;
* :func:`train_gene_graph` runs the models: a graph transformer (``gps``),
  GraphSAGE (``sage``), GCN (``gcn``), Hadamard logistic regression (``lr``)
  and a Laplacian-eigenmap embedding (``spectral``), plus the training-free
  baselines ``cosine``, ``adamicadar`` and ``prior``, each over feature arms
  and under the controls ``shufX`` (features permuted among genes),
  ``shufY`` (labels relabelled by a gene permutation) and ``rewire``
  (degree-preserving swaps);
* :func:`evaluate_gene_graph` writes the time-split and held-out metrics,
  the per-fold summaries, the ablation table and the paired fold deltas;
* :func:`predict_gene_functions` calibrates the out-of-fold scores, controls
  the false discovery rate with the non-targeting pseudo-genes as decoys and
  writes the explained prediction lists.

The models are plain PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy and scikit-learn. They run on the
device named by ``gene_graph_device``; a CUDA device that is not available
falls back to the CPU. On CUDA, the card rule of the shared workstation
applies: a run waits until the card total plus its cap stays below
``gene_graph_gpu_limit_gb`` for ``gene_graph_admission_hold_s`` seconds,
yields (saving a resume file) when the card goes over the limit, and stops
when ``gene_graph_gpu_budget_h`` GPU hours are used. On the CPU the
computation is deterministic, so a rerun from the saved settings file
writes the same tables.

spacr.gene_knowledge:
Protein-knowledge feature blocks for gene-level analysis, built so they cannot leak the answer.

What a screen adds to gene-function prediction can only be stated against
what prior protein knowledge alone predicts. This module builds that
knowledge on the gene graph's node order (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`): one row
per screen gene and one per non-targeting pseudo-gene.

* :func:`fetch_protein_annotations`: UniProt sequences, Pfam / InterPro
  cross-references and function text, current (REST, batches of at most 100
  accessions) and from an archived Swiss-Prot release (``.dat`` streamed out
  of the release tarball); plus a seeded draw of reviewed human proteins
  outside the library, the decoys' knowledge;
* :func:`embed_sequences`: ESM-2 mean residue embeddings, long sequences in
  overlapping windows;
* :func:`embed_text`: function sentences, each with the gene symbols and
  accessions it names, embedded by a local sentence model (mean pooling,
  L2-normalised);
* :func:`predict_3di`: the ProstT5 encoder and its CNN head predict a 3Di
  structure string per sequence, and the 3Di string is embedded;
* :func:`foldseek_similarity`: an all-vs-all Foldseek search gives the
  structural-similarity edges and the paralog pairs;
* :func:`build_knowledge_blocks`: the per-task blocks (text masked per fold,
  ``_time`` blocks from the archive only), decoy blocks and structure blocks;
* :func:`paralog_mask` and :func:`profile_metrics`.

Leakage rules enforced here: in fold ``k`` the fold's genes and decoys get no
text vector and every sentence of any other gene naming a fold-``k`` gene is
dropped before averaging, with the text PCA refit per fold; ``_time`` blocks
read only the archive; sequence, domain and structure blocks are kept for
held-out genes, domain names are never embedded and GO is never an input;
decoys carry an out-of-library protein's knowledge; Foldseek edges are
message-passing inputs only.

No hosted model or API is used. Models run from local Hugging Face weights
(``gene_knowledge_models_dir``); they are downloaded only when
``gene_knowledge_allow_download`` is on. Every step can instead reuse the
stored output of an earlier run (``*_embeddings``, ``*_outputs``,
``foldseek_alignments``), which is how a run is repeated without a GPU.

spacr.gpu_admission:
Wait until the GPU is free before a long run takes it (item 872, B11 and B19, alpha).

A plate-scale phenotype run holds the card for days, so it must not start
while another job is using it, and it must give the card back cleanly. The
reference launcher of the Funk et al. 2022 run did this in a shell script;
:class:`GpuAdmission` is that behaviour as a policy that can be tested
without a GPU:

* optionally wait for another job's release line in a file;
* then wait for ``idle_checks`` samples in a row in which the card shows 0 %
  utilisation and no running compute process uses more than
  ``min_process_mib``. Display and browser processes never count
  (``ignore_patterns``: a browser's ``--type=gpu-process`` held about
  600 MiB and blocked the reference launcher for hours), and nor do stopped
  processes;
* write ``START`` and ``FINISH`` lines to ``~/.spacr/gpu/log``;
* stop cleanly when a ``STOP`` file appears;
* hand out fewer measurement workers when the card's memory in use is above
  a cap (:meth:`GpuAdmission.workers_under_cap`).

The device is queried through ``nvidia-smi`` by :func:`query_gpu`; every
part of the policy takes the query, the clock and the sleep as arguments, so
a test fakes the device.

spacr.ops_modules:
Gene modules of an optical pooled screen: consensus clusters with a known core.

A module is a cluster of the reference clustering that is anchored by known
biology (a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway or a GO-slim term enriched in it),
together with the genes the screen places next to that core although no
resource links them to it. The atlas is built in three steps.

1. **Partitions.** The gene profiles (targeting genes with more than ten
   cells, plus the control guides grouped at random into pseudo-genes of
   four, :func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_rows`) are clustered once with
   PHATE + Leiden (seed 42) at the resolutions of :data:`MODULE_RESOLUTIONS`
   (about 70, 250 and 500 clusters), and again ``ops_modules_runs`` times on
   resampled rows and guides (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_run`).
   By default the profiles are standardised and reduced to the components
   holding 99 % of the variance first. With
   ``ops_modules_precomputed_embedding`` the profile columns are used as
   they are, which is what a weighted profile (contrastive weighting) needs:
   standardising it again would undo the weighting.
2. **Anchoring.** In every reference cluster, a one-sided Fisher test for
   every group of 3 to 500 clustered genes, Benjamini-Hochberg within the
   cluster; the best group with q < 0.05 and three or more cluster genes is
   the anchor and its cluster genes are the known core.
3. **Gates.** A gene not linked to the core (no STRING v12 link of 0.4 or
   more, no BioGRID physical interaction, no shared enriched group) is a
   stable new member when its co-membership with the core over the
   consensus runs is above 0.5 and above the 99th percentile of both the
   control pseudo-genes and 500 fitness-matched random genes, its mean cosine
   to the core is above that of 1,000 fitness-matched genes (p < 0.01), at
   least three of its four guides point at the core, and its guides carry no
   specificity flag.

Controls: the control pseudo-genes pass through the same gates (empirical
FDR), and the gene labels are shuffled three times among the targeting rows
and the anchoring and gates recomputed on the same partitions.

This is the plate A pilot's module atlas; every seed is the pilot's, so a
settings run gives the pilot's partitions and tables. PHATE and Leiden come
with the ``clustering`` extra, ``pip install "spacr[clustering]"``.

spacr.ops_run_infra:
Run infrastructure of the OPS phenotype path at plate scale (item 872, alpha).

The large Funk et al. 2022 phenotype run (plates LaC024A-D, about 1,280
fields of 2,960 px per well) found engineering limits that the phase code in
:mod:`spacr.ops_engine` alone does not address. This module holds the parts
that are not phases themselves:

* :class:`FieldStager` reads raw phenotype fields from network storage ahead
  of the run with a few threads, keeps only each field's maximum projection
  on local disk, and deletes it once the field is done, so each raw file is
  read once and local space stays bounded (B2);
* :func:`compare_tables` is the GPU-against-CPU self-check of one measured
  field (B7);
* :func:`archive_well`, :func:`archived_well` and :func:`mark_plate_done`
  copy a finished well to archive storage, verify the copy by size and MD5
  and write the ``WELL_DONE`` / ``PLATE_DONE`` markers a resumed run starts
  from (B9);
* :func:`crop_index` and :func:`stream_crops` read the sharded crop store
  whole shard by whole shard, shuffled within and between shards, as a
  training loader does (WebDataset style; Aizman et al. 2019,
  arXiv:2001.01858) (B16);
* :func:`integer_cell_key` is the integer join key of the measurement
  tables (B17);
* :func:`stress_rows` measures a finished run's store the way the reference
  stress test did and :func:`write_stress_report` writes
  ``results/ops_stress/stress_test.csv`` (B20).

Every function is deterministic for the same inputs except the timings the
stress report records, which depend on the machine.

  so ``gen_mask_settings.csv`` holds the whole mask run;
* ``measure``: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop`;
* ``export``: :func:`export_plate_parquet` turns ``measurements.db`` into
  one per-cell Parquet file per plate and writes each field's cell counts
  to the ``image`` table;
* ``aggregate``: :func:`aggregate_wells` writes the well means, medians,
  per-well heterogeneity and the control cells' percentiles.

With ``record_timing`` each phase's wall and CPU seconds go to
``<src>/settings/screen_timing.json``.

The mask phases take the mask settings from the file and the measure phase
the measure settings; a key both pipelines read (``channels``, ``n_jobs``)
goes to both, except ``normalize``, which means something different in
each and so is left to the measure defaults. ``mask_overrides`` and
``measure_overrides`` set a key for one phase alone, such as::

    run_screen({'src': 'work/Week10_40111',
                'import_source': 'images/Week10_40111',
                'channels': [0, 1, 2], 'nucleus_channel': 0, 'cell_channel': 1,
                'magnification': 20,
                'mask_overrides': {'illumination_correction': False},
                'measure_overrides': {'illumination_correction': True,
                                      'cell_min_size': 177,
                                      'nucleus_min_size': 177},
                'aggregate_metadata': 'BBBC021_v1_image.csv',
                'aggregate_metadata_columns': 'Image_Metadata_Plate_DAPI,'
                                              'Image_Metadata_Well_DAPI,'
                                              'Image_Metadata_Compound'})

``spacr-run screen --settings plate.csv`` does the same from a file.
spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells:
Aggregate per-cell plate files into well tables.

Each plate file is aggregated on its own (a well lies on one plate) by
``plate`` and ``well`` over its ``cell_``, ``nucleus_``, ``cytoplasm_``
and ``pathogen_`` columns:

* ``wells_mean.parquet`` / ``wells_median.parquet``: the mean or median
  of every feature, with ``n_cells``;
* ``wells_heterogeneity.parquet``: each feature's standard deviation
  (``<feature>__sd``) and 10-90% spread (``<feature>__p90mp10``), with
  ``n_cells``;
* ``<control>_percentiles.parquet`` (such as
  ``dmso_percentiles.parquet``) when ``controls`` are given: per plate
  and quantile ``q``, the percentile of every feature over the control
  wells' cells, the reference of Ljosa et al. 2013's scaling
  (:func:`spacr.sp_stats._normalize_profiles`, ``ljosa_percentile``).

:param parquet_files: the per-plate files of :func:`export_plate_parquet`.
:param dst: the output folder; created if absent.
:param levels: ``'well_mean'`` and/or ``'well_median'``.
:param controls: the control ``(plate, well)`` pairs (see
    :func:`control_wells`); ``None`` writes no percentiles.
:param control_name: names the percentile file.
:param percentiles: the percentiles to write, such as ``(1, 99)``.
:param heterogeneity: also write the heterogeneity table.
:param prefixes: the prefixes of the feature columns; the embedding
    aggregate (item 896) passes ``('emb_',)``.
:returns: ``{"paths", "plates", "n_cells", "n_features"}``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown level, no input files, or files
    without feature columns.

The ``(plate, well)`` pairs of a metadata table whose treatment is the control.

spacr.screen_staging.export_plate_parque:
Turn a plate's ``measurements.db`` into one Parquet file with one row per cell.

Cell and cytoplasm rows share ``(prcf, object_label)``; nucleus rows
name their cell in ``cell_id``. A cell with several nuclei gets the
features of its largest nucleus and ``Metadata_n_nuclei``; nuclei
without a cell are not exported. The keys are ``plate``, ``well``
(such as B02), ``site`` and ``Metadata_cell_id``; positions
(centroids, bounding boxes, distance to the field edge) are kept as
``Location_*`` columns so profile scorers skip them, and bookkeeping
columns are dropped, as are the ``pathogen`` distance features a plate
without a pathogen table carries. Features are ``float32``.

With ``write_image_counts`` each field's ``n_cells``,
``cells_without_nucleus`` and ``cells_multi_nucleus`` are written to the
``image`` table of ``measurements.db`` (item 814).

:param src: the plate folder holding ``measurements/measurements.db``.
:param dst: the Parquet folder; ``None`` writes to ``<src>/parquet``.
:param plate: the plate name for the file and the ``plate`` column;
    ``None`` takes the database's one plate.
:param write_image_counts: write the per-field counts to ``image``.
:returns: the export record: ``path``, ``n_cells``, ``n_cells_db``,
    ``n_features``, ``n_fields``, ``n_wells``, ``tables`` and, with a
    nucleus table, ``n_nuclei_db``, ``nuclei_without_cell``,
    ``cells_without_nucleus`` and ``cells_multi_nucleus``.
:raises ValueError: when the database is missing, holds no cell table,
    repeats a cell, or holds more than one plate.

to ``src/orig`` by the mask pipeline, is left as it is, so an import can

The settings of :func:`run_screen`, filled in with their defaults.

Holds the mask pipeline's keys, the measure pipeline's keys and this
module's own; a key the two pipelines share takes the mask default.

:param settings: settings given so far; a key already present is kept.
:returns: a new dict with every key :func:`run_screen` reads.
spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation:
Score well profiles by mechanism of action under NSC and NSCB, over several seeds.

The BBBC021 benchmark (Ljosa et al. 2013) as the reanalysis's scorer of
record runs it (``run_and_score.py`` and ``supervised_moa.py``):

1. every well gets its plate, well, compound and concentration (from
   ``metadata`` when the profiles lack them) and every numeric column
   outside the keys, counts and ``moa_eval_exclude`` is a feature;
2. each plate is normalised to its control wells (``moa_eval_normalise``)
   and a feature without a finite positive scale on some plate is
   dropped; ``moa_eval_feature_qc='standard'`` then drops a feature
   non-finite in more than 5% of wells or above 500 after
   normalisation (pycytominer's drop_na_columns and drop_outliers, item
   807);
3. the labelled wells (``moa_eval_labels``, controls left out) are
   scored by each method of ``moa_eval_methods``, leaving one compound
   out (:mod:`spacr.moa_benchmark`): ``1nn_cosine`` on treatment
   profiles (replicate wells combined by ``moa_eval_replicates``),
   and the supervised ``logistic``, ``xgboost``, ``lda``,
   ``shrinkage_lda``, ``knn`` and the nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5
   classifiers ``cpa_<name>`` (:mod:`spacr.cpa_classifiers`) on the
   wells, as ``float32``;
4. per seed the supervised fits use that seed, and the shuffled-label
   control permutes the compound-to-MoA mapping with generator seed
   ``seed + 1`` and refits with seeds ``seed + 1 + i`` (the reference's
   convention at seed 0); the 1-NN control uses generator seed
   ``seed``. The majority-class control counts the treatments the
   first method scored.

:param profiles: one row per well, a frame or a table path, with
    ``plate`` and ``well``.
:param metadata: a frame or table path naming each well's compound and
    concentration, by ``moa_eval_metadata_columns``; ``None`` when the
    profiles carry them.
:param settings: the keys of
    :func:`spacr.moa_benchmark.profiling_evaluation_defaults`.
:returns: ``{"summary", "controls", "per_moa", "confusion",
    "predictions", "features", "dropped", "qc_dropped"}``: accuracy per
    method, protocol and seed; the control rows; the per-MoA accuracy;
    ``{method: long confusion table}``; every prediction; the scored
    features; the features normalisation dropped and the ones the QC
    dropped.
:raises _ProfilingError: for an unknown normalisation, method or
    protocol, or missing metadata, percentiles or control wells.
spacr.well_set_training:
Train and score the spaCR well transformer on per-cell embeddings, with its ablations and controls.

A well is a set of single-cell embeddings (such as the per-channel ResNet-18
embeddings :mod:`spacr.embedding_profiles` writes, ``<plate>.npy`` beside
the crop index ``<plate>.cells.parquet``). This module trains the
:class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer` on those sets, the way the
BMC reanalysis ``train_well.py`` did, and scores it on BBBC021-style
mechanism-of-action (MoA) folds:

1. :func:`load_cell_embeddings` reads the embeddings and normalises them
   without labels (``train_set_normalisation``): ``'plate_control_pca'``
   centres and scales every dimension per plate by that plate's control
   (DMSO) cells, then whitens with a PCA fitted on control cells of all
   plates (typical-variation-normalisation-like, Ando et al. 2017); the
   control is the negative control on every plate, so using it on test
   plates is not label leakage. ``'plate_control'`` stops after the plate
   step and ``'none'`` keeps the embeddings as they are.
2. :func:`group_wells` groups the cells into wells, and :func:`moa_folds`
   gives the folds of ``train_protocol``: ``'NSCB'`` (not same compound or
   batch: one fold per batch, plus the taxol 1 and 3 uM fold) or ``'NSC'``
   (not same compound: four folds, every compound of a MoA in another fold).
3. :func:`train_arrayed` trains one arm per fold, and :func:`predict_arrayed`
   predicts the test wells. Arms (:data:`WELL_SET_ARMS`): ``settf`` (ISAB set
   encoder and gated attention-MIL), ``abmil`` (attention-MIL only), ``n1``
   (set size 1 in training and test, the well being the mean of its cells'
   softmax: the no-context ablation), ``mixbag`` (bags drawn from cells of
   random training wells of the same class, which keeps the label but breaks
   within-well co-occurrence), ``mean_lr`` (mean profile and logistic
   regression) and ``mean_knn`` (mean profile and cosine 1-NN on treatment
   profiles, the classic BBBC021 baseline).
4. :func:`score_treatments` scores the wells as the reference
   ``eval_bbbc.py`` does: well softmax with untrained classes zeroed,
   treatment mean, argmax; accuracy with a bootstrap confidence interval
   over treatments, macro AUROC and macro AP.

:func:`run_well_set_arm` runs one arm from a config dict;
:func:`run_well_set_training` runs every arm of ``train_set_arms`` from the
settings of :mod:`spacr.architecture_training`, with the shuffled-label control (``train_set_shuffle_control``: the
compound to MoA map is permuted) and the majority-class control, and writes
``summary.csv`` with one row per arm and control. Synthetic data with known
penetrance (:func:`synthetic_arrayed`) and with a well batch effect
(:func:`synthetic_pooled`) check the arrayed and the pooled mode on the CPU.

Everything is seeded: ``train_set_seed`` seeds torch once per arm before the
first fold, and numpy generators seed the bag draws, so a rerun with the same
thread count gives the same table.

The :func:`run_well_set_arm` config of one arm from settings.

:param settings: the keys of :func:`well_set_defaults`.
:param arm: one of :data:`WELL_SET_ARMS`.
:param shuffled: the shuffled-label control of the arm.

A LambdaLR with a linear warm-up over ``warm_frac`` of the steps and a cosine decay.

:param opt: the optimiser.
:param steps: total steps.
:param warm_frac: share of the steps spent warming up (at least one step).
:returns: the scheduler.
spacr.well_set_training.group_wells:
One row per well, in order of first appearance, with the row numbers of its cells.

:param cells: cell table with plate, well, compound, concentration, moa and week.
:returns: a well table with those columns, ``n`` (cells) and ``rows`` (an array of cell rows).
spacr.well_set_training.load_cell_embedd:
Read per-plate embeddings and their cell tables, and normalise them.

:param embeddings: folder of ``<plate>.npy``, read in sorted order.
:param cells: folder of ``<plate>.cells.parquet``; None uses ``embeddings``.
:param method: one of :data:`NORMALISATIONS`.
:param pca_dims: dimensions kept by the PCA.
:param control: MoA value of the control cells.
:returns: the cell table (plate, well, compound, concentration, moa and
    ``week``, the plate name up to its first underscore) and the
    normalised embeddings, row-aligned.
:raises FileNotFoundError: no ``.npy`` file in ``embeddings``.
spacr.well_set_training.make_pooled_batc:
Disjoint target and context cells per well.

:param rng: numpy generator.
:param cells_by_well: the cell rows of each well.
:param wells: the wells of the batch.
:param T: targets per well.
:param Mctx: context cells per well.
:param tgt_ok: per cell, may it be a target.
:param ctx_ok: per cell, may it be context.
:param ctx_mode: ``'same'`` (other cells of the same well), ``'none'`` or ``'other'`` (a random other well).
:param all_wells: the wells ``'other'`` draws from.
:returns: the target rows and the context rows of each well; a target is never in its own context.
spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds:
The folds of a fold protocol over labelled wells, as the BBBC021 CNN reference defines them.

``'NSCB'``: one fold per batch (``week``, ordered by its number), testing
that week's non-taxol wells and training on every other week; then a
taxol fold, testing taxol at 1 and 3 uM and training on the non-taxol
wells of the other weeks. ``'NSC'``: four folds; within each MoA the
compounds are dealt to folds 0, 1, 2, 3 in a permutation drawn with seed 0.

:param wells: labelled wells with compound, week, concentration and moa.
:param protocol: one of :data:`PROTOCOLS` (``'NSC_A'`` is accepted for ``'NSC'``).
:returns: ``(name, train mask, test mask)`` per fold.
:raises ValueError: an unknown protocol.
spacr.well_set_training.normalise_embedd:
Normalise per-plate cell embeddings without labels.

:param blocks: one ``(cells, dims)`` array per plate.
:param tables: the matching cell tables, with ``moa_column``.
:param method: one of :data:`NORMALISATIONS`.
:param pca_dims: dimensions kept by the PCA whitening.
:param control: value of ``moa_column`` of the control cells.
:param moa_column: column naming each cell's MoA.
:param sample: at most this many control cells fit the PCA (drawn with ``seed``).
:param seed: seed of that draw.
:returns: the concatenated embeddings, float16 after the PCA and float32 otherwise.
:raises ValueError: an unknown method, a table and block of different lengths, or a plate without control cells.
spacr.well_set_training.pad_bags:
Stack bags of cell rows into one zero-padded batch.

:param dev: torch device.
:returns: the ``(B, N, D)`` batch and its ``(B, N)`` validity mask.
spacr.well_set_training.pooled_forward:
Logits of the target cells given their contexts.

:param model: a pooled well transformer.
:param X: cell embeddings.
:param tg: target rows per well.
:param cx: context rows per well (may be empty).
:param dev: torch device.
:returns: the ``(B, T, K)`` logits and the target validity mask.
spacr.well_set_training.predict_arrayed:
Predict wells with a trained arrayed arm.

:param X: cell embeddings.

:param wells: the wells to predict.

spacr.well_set_training.run_synthetic_ar:
Train and score an arrayed arm on :func:`synthetic_arrayed` (every fifth well tested).

    Pearson r and mean absolute error and the median ratio of attention

Train and score a pooled arm on :func:`synthetic_pooled`, half of every well's cells held out.

    batch_sd and sep.

spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_arm:
Train and score one arm over every fold of a protocol.

    ``threads``, ``folds`` (fold numbers to run, or None), ``control``,

    :func:`train_arrayed`.

:param Z: the normalised embeddings.

:param log: called with keyword events (per fold and every 250 steps).
:returns: the summary dict of the arm (as the reference ``summary.json``).

spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_tra:
Run every arm of ``train_set_arms`` from settings and write the results.

Each arm gets its folder ``<dst>/<run>/`` with config.json,
summary.json, treatment_probs.csv and (transformer arms)
well_penetrance.csv; ``<dst>/summary.csv`` has one row per arm, per

    image architecture (those train on crops: :mod:`spacr.channel_pretraining`).
spacr.well_set_training.score_treatments:
Score well probabilities per treatment.

Wells are averaged per treatment (compound, concentration, MoA and fold),
the treatment takes the MoA of its largest mean probability, and the
accuracy gets a percentile bootstrap interval over treatments.

:param wells: the scored wells with plate, well, compound, concentration, moa and fold.
:param P: their probabilities, untrained classes already zeroed (:func:`zero_untrained`).
:param classes: the class names of the columns of ``P``.

One ``summary.csv`` row from an arm's summary dict.

:returns: the row, in :data:`SUMMARY_COLUMNS`.
spacr.well_set_training.synthetic_arraye:
Synthetic arrayed wells with a known penetrance.

Each well has one class; a well-specific fraction of its cells, uniform
on ``pen_range``, is shifted along the class direction and the rest look
like controls, plus a per-well batch offset.

:param seed: numpy seed.
:param n_wells: wells (well ``w`` has class ``w % K``).
:param K: classes.
:param D: embedding dimension.
:param cells: range of cells per well.
:param pen_range: range of the penetrant fraction.
:param shift: length of the class shift.
:returns: the embeddings, the cell rows of each well, the well labels,
    the true penetrance, the per-cell penetrant flag and 4,000 control cells.
spacr.well_set_training.synthetic_pooled:
Synthetic pooled wells: every well mixes all classes under a strong per-well batch offset.

:param seed: numpy seed.
:param n_wells: wells.
:param cells: cells per well.
:param K: classes.
:param D: embedding dimension.
:param batch_sd: size of the per-well offset a no-context model cannot remove.
:param sep: class separation.

spacr.well_set_training.train_arrayed:
Train one arrayed arm on the training wells of a fold.

Every step draws ``bag_batch`` classes uniformly, a training well of each
and a bag of ``bag_cells`` cells of it (``n1``: one cell; ``mixbag``:
cells from ``mixbag_pool``). The loss is the label-smoothed well

with AdamW, gradient clipping at 1 and :func:`cosine_schedule`.

:param cfg: the arm config: arm, steps, bag_batch, bag_cells, dim, depth,
    lr, weight_decay, instance_weight and seed.
:param X: cell embeddings.
:param w_rows: the cell rows of each well.
:param y_well: the class of each well.
:param n_cls: classes.
:param train_w: the training wells.
:param dev: torch device.
:param log: called with keyword events every 250 steps.
:param mixbag_pool: per class, the cell rows of its training wells (``mixbag`` only).
:returns: the trained model.
spacr.well_set_training.well_set_default:
The settings of :func:`run_well_set_training`, filled in with their defaults.

spacr.well_set_training.zero_untrained:
